frequency_question: How often does institutional and legal friction block or delay the implementation of announced major executive tariffs before the deadline?
membership_rule: Includes unilateral executive tariff announcements with defined short timelines; excludes congressional statutes and broad multi-year trade negotiations.
coverage_note: 5 named major high-profile executive tariff threats with short windows; captures the friction class.
known_gaps: Excludes minor product-specific exclusions processing delays which do not stop the overarching tariff.
skeleton: Executive trade actions announced with short deadlines vs. those successfully delayed or negotiated away by institutional friction.
multiplier: 3 hits / 5 total historical precedent actions = 60% base rate of implementation despite friction.
validity_reason: Statutory authorities like Section 232 and 301 remain stable across presidential administrations, preserving the friction architecture.
